details.label: Summary
details.text: Some increase in storm coverage and severe potential is possible with time this morning

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple storm clusters are approaching the Lower Great Lakes vicinity early this morning. The downstream environment remains generally favorable for organized convection, with MUCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg and effective shear of 35-45 kt. Large-scale ascent is generally rather modest, though low-level warm advection may help to sustain the ongoing storm clusters through dawn. Short-term severe potential remains uncertain with the ongoing storms. The cluster mode and generally modest midlevel lapse rates are not particularly favorable for hail, while low-level stability may temper severe-wind potential downstream of the lakes. As a result, the wind-damage and hail potential may tend to remain rather isolated. If any of these clusters are able to persist into mid morning and beyond, then diurnal heating/destabilization may allow for intensification and an increasing downstream severe threat
